title: wave next strict-parses the policy before its own build step, so a batch that adds a policy key bricks the next boundary
summary: On 2026-10-21, after batch three (#1097) merged, `evolve wave next --json` exited rc=2 with `policy: parse .../.evolve/policy.json: cli_routing: tier rule: ... json: unknown field "share_pct"`. sync-main had brought in the new policy key of #1068, but the runtime binary was the build from before the batch. wave next strict-parses the policy in prepareWave before its own wave-build step, so the console had to run `make -C go build` by hand first.
fix: Before the first strict policy parse, a non-dry wave next runs the boot refresh of the loop (bootBinaryRefresh, cmd_loop_boot_refresh.go): a binary behind HEAD with a go/ delta is rebuilt and the process re-execs into it. When the parse still meets an unknown field, the error names the remedy: make -C <root>/go build, then run wave next again.
acceptance: A wave next whose synced policy carries a key that the binary does not know rebuilds and re-execs before the policy parse and before any boundary step (TestWaveNext_APolicyKeyTheBinaryDoesNotKnowRebuildsAndReExecsBeforeTheParse).
A fresh binary launches with no rebuild (TestWaveNext_AFreshBinaryLaunchesWithNoRebuild); a dry run never rebuilds (TestWaveNext_ADryRunNeverRebuildsTheBinary).
An unknown policy key names the rebuild remedy; another parse error keeps its own text (TestWaveNext_AnUnknownPolicyKeyNamesTheRebuildRemedy, TestWaveNext_AnotherPolicyErrorKeepsItsOwnText).
The opt-out boot.binary_refresh=off holds also when the policy has an unknown key (TestWaveNext_TheRefreshOptOutHoldsWhenThePolicyHasAnUnknownKey).
The fix reuses bootBinaryRefresh; no second self-heal mechanism.
routed_reason: boundary tooling (wave next) that the console runs; a lane cannot run a boundary

consumed.resolution: wave next runs bootBinaryRefresh before the policy parse (rebuild and re-exec of a stale plane binary); an unknown-field policy error names make -C <root>/go build
